$comment: OWNER-AUTHORIZED manager role grants, sandbox only. Prepared 2026-08-19.
Owner authorization (verbatim, 2026-08-19): 'make this happen Mike -> operationsManager .
Santana -> salesManager . Erik -> accountingManager . Jake -> fieldManager', subsequently
CORRECTED by the Owner to: 'Santaana should be sales manager role. Erik should be finance
manager role, jake should be service manager role.'
Owner ruling #113 (2026-08-19) requires this manifest to exist before any provisioning write:
'No provisioning or activation writes without a dry-run manifest and separate sandbox
authorization.' This file is that manifest. It does NOT perform the grant -- assignApprovedRole
/ grantRole are deployed Cloud Functions and calling them is a separate protected action.
TWO NAMING DISCREPANCIES ARE RESOLVED HERE, DELIBERATELY, AND NEITHER IS A SILENT SUBSTITUTION:
1. Erik. The Owner's first message said accountingManager; the correction said financeManager.
The correction governs, so financeManager is what this manifest grants. Note the two Roles
are now INTENTIONALLY IDENTICAL in capability (DECISIONS #114, PR #1314), so this choice
changes nothing about what Erik can do today -- it only records which Role he holds. His Auth
displayName is still 'Erik Accounting Manager', which now disagrees with his Role; renaming a
display name is a separate write and is NOT included here.
2. Jake. The Owner asked for 'service manager role'. There is NO serviceManager among the 15
governed business Roles. fieldManager IS that Role: it carries the full Work Order lifecycle
(workOrder.create/transition/cancel) plus inventory.transaction.read, coordinated-visit read,
and account.record.read. This was confirmed with the Owner before implementation, after an
earlier report of fieldManager's contents was found to be wrong (a grep pattern that excluded
camelCase capability ids). Granting fieldManager is the faithful reading of the instruction,
not a substitution made for convenience.
PRECONDITIONS VERIFIED LIVE against eos-platform-sandbox on 2026-08-19, read-only:
- all four employee documents exist
- all four users documents exist and resolve to the principalUid recorded below
- NONE of the four already holds the Role being granted (no duplicate/no-op writes)
- 10 active roleAssignments exist before this change; 14 expected after
GRANT IS NOT ACTIVATION. Several capabilities these Roles carry are registered active:false
(salesOrder.read, fulfillment.coordinatedVisit.read). Granting the Role records the authority;
those ids still resolve DENY until per-environment activation. Nothing here activates anything.
SCOPE. Sandbox only. These four principals exist only in eos-platform-sandbox. This manifest
confers no production authority and must never be replayed against taylor-parts.
authorizationReference: Owner instruction 2026-08-19 ('make this happen') as corrected same day; Owner ruling #113 (docs/DECISIONS.md) authorising all 15 governed business Roles to be grantable
preparedBy: Claude Opus 5, repository prepare-lane only (no write performed)

grants.businessNeed: Cross-domain operational oversight across Customer, Service, Inventory, Warehouse and Purchasing. Owner-named operations manager for the sandbox evaluation. Carries no role administration, no governed-field write and no reorder decision authority; can open a Customer but not amend one (deliberate asymmetry, DECISIONS #114).

Customer/CRM read, create and update, plus Sales Order read and inventory visibility (Owner ruling 2026-08-19). Owner-named sales manager. salesOrder.read is registered active:false and remains inert until per-environment activation.

Financial oversight: Customer read, governed commercial-field write (Issue #175), and both sides of the committed-money picture -- Sales Orders out and Purchase Orders in (Owner ruling 2026-08-19). Owner corrected the Role from accountingManager to financeManager; the two are intentionally identical in capability per DECISIONS #114.

Technicians, dispatch and Work Orders: full Work Order lifecycle authority (create/transition/cancel), field-inventory read, coordinated-visit read and Customer read. This is the Role the Owner meant by 'service manager'; no serviceManager Role exists.

notIncluded: inventoryCreateExecutor -- Owner ruling #113 withholds it until an exact recipient and business need are presented. Owner answered 'Non one' when asked. Not granted.

owner -- no owner roleAssignment exists for any principal, which is why Reporting is unreachable and owner >= admin does not hold in practice. Granting it is privileged and requires a second distinct approver (two-person rule); it is deliberately NOT bundled into this manifest.
Display-name corrections -- Erik's Auth displayName still reads 'Accounting Manager' against a financeManager Role. Cosmetic, a separate write, not included.
Warehouse assignments -- tracked separately in warehouse-assignment-manifest-2026-08-19.json; no employee currently has one, so every warehouse-scoped predicate still denies for everyone.
